title: Haplotypes: V K O R C one and T P M T star three A

segs.text: Section three. Haplotype nomenclature. A haplotype is a set of variants at several positions, called loci, on one allele that occur together more often than chance. A combination that keeps turning up is worth one name, easier to say than the list of changes. Whoever discovers a haplotype names it, so naming differs from gene to gene.

V K O R C one has at least ten S N Ps that may have a functional effect, grouped in different ways. She said, There's one called haplotype A, and there's another called haplotype B. Haplotype B is the most common, and these haplotypes matter for their functional significance.

T P M T, thiopurine methyltransferase, uses a star name with a letter. The allele was first called star three. She said, We did some more work and realized that three is actually two snips in the gene. So it became star three A. The two changes are six fifteen, G to A, and eight seventy four, A to G. Together they give significantly reduced T P M T activity, which matters for azathioprine and six mercaptopurine.
A haplotype is not a genotype. A haplotype is several variants on one allele, such as the two changes in star three A. A genotype is the pair of alleles a person carries, one from each parent.
